hypothesis: A source-bound witness of the actual fit call detects mismatches between data used for fitting and declared fit IDs that a metadata-only overlap checker may miss.

scenarios.name: clean
scenarios.description: Estimator actually fit only train rows using correct train IDs.

scenarios.name: fit_evaluation_truthful_ids
scenarios.description: Estimator fit on train+evaluation rows with their true IDs; metadata supplied correctly includes evaluation IDs.

scenarios.name: fit_evaluation_false_ids
scenarios.description: Estimator fit on evaluation values only, but row IDs are drawn from the train partition and no eval overlap is declared.

scenarios.name: fit_evaluation_true_trace_false_metadata
scenarios.description: Estimator fit on evaluation values, trace has real evaluation IDs, but separate manual fit ID declaration claims only train.

scenarios.name: without_witness
scenarios.description: Estimator trained directly outside the recorder, no source witness available.

guardrails: Models may be fitted on evaluation data only in intentionally broken experiment branches; their scores must not be reported as generalization results.
A caller can forge both row IDs and numeric data. Witnesses are local snapshots, not independent third-party attestations.
Missing witness evidence must be UNKNOWN, not OK.
An internally consistent hash does not establish legitimate source origin.
Scenarios within the same dataset share samples and are correlated.
No observer component may train, repair, or change a model automatically.
The recorder forwards a caller explicitly initiated fit call and records it; that is distinct from autonomous observer training.
Do not claim novel detection relative to a baseline with equally rich authenticated fit traces.
